complications.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
complications.source_text: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is diagnosed by the persistent elevation of urinary albumin excretion (albuminuria), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73 m², or other manifestations of kidney damage (1).

complications.name: CKD Stage G3
complications.source_text: Complications of chronic kidney disease (CKD) generally become prevalent when estimated glomerular filtration rate falls below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² (stage G3 CKD or greater) and become more common and severe as CKD progresses.

complications.name: CKD Stage G4
complications.source_text: Consultation with a nephrologist when stage G4 CKD develops (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²) has been found to reduce cost, improve quality of care, and delay the need for dialysis (159).

complications.name: Acute Kidney Injury
complications.source_text: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is defined as a rapid decline in kidney function, typically within a short period (hours to days), characterized by increase in serum creatinine and/or decrease in urine output (26).

complications.name: Cardiovascular Disease (CVD)
complications.source_text: In addition, among people with type 1 or type 2 diabetes, the presence of CKD markedly increases cardiovascular risk and health care costs (6).

complications.name: Diabetic Retinopathy
complications.source_text: The typical presentation of CKD in people with diabetes is considered to include long-standing duration of diabetes, retinopathy, albuminuria without gross hematuria, and gradually progressive loss of eGFR. However, signs of CKD may be present at diagnosis or without retinopathy in type 2 diabetes.

complications.name: Nephrotic syndrome
complications.source_text: the presence of nephrotic syndrome, rapidly decreasing eGFR, or the absence of retinopathy (particularly in type 1 diabetes) suggests alternative or additional causes of kidney disease.

screening_tests.name: Urine Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (UACR)
screening_tests.source_text: Assess kidney function with random urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at least annually in people with type 1 diabetes with duration of ≥5 years and in all people with type 2 diabetes regardless of treatment. B
screening_tests.indication: Assess kidney function in people with type 1 diabetes (duration ≥5 years) and all people with type 2 diabetes.

screening_tests.name: Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR)
screening_tests.source_text: Assess kidney function with random urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at least annually in people with type 1 diabetes with duration of ≥5 years and in all people with type 2 diabetes regardless of treatment. B
screening_tests.indication: Assess kidney function in people with type 1 diabetes (duration ≥5 years) and all people with type 2 diabetes.

screening_tests.name: Spot Urine Albumin
screening_tests.source_text: In people with chronic kidney disease (CKD), monitor urinary albumin (e.g., spot UACR) and eGFR 1–4 times per year depending on the stage of kidney disease (Fig. 11.1). B
screening_tests.indication: Monitor urinary albumin in people with CKD.

screening_tests.name: Serum electrolytes
screening_tests.frequency: Every 6-12 months for stage G3 CKD, every 3-5 months for stage G4 CKD, and every 1-3 months for stage G5 CKD

screening_tests.name: Hemoglobin testing
screening_tests.source_text:
Anemia
Hemoglobin; iron, iron saturation, ferritin testing if indicated
screening_tests.frequency: Every 6-12 months for stage G3 CKD, every 3-5 months for stage G4 CKD, and every 1-3 months for stage G5 CKD

screening_tests.name: Iron testing
screening_tests.source_text:

screening_tests.name: Serum calcium, phosphate, PTH, vitamin 25(OH)D
screening_tests.source_text:
Metabolic bone disease
Serum calcium, phosphate, PTH, vitamin 25(OH)D
screening_tests.frequency: Every 6-12 months for stage G3 CKD, every 3-5 months for stage G4 CKD, and every 1-3 months for stage G5 CKD

screening_tests.name: Serum potassium
screening_tests.source_text: Serum potassium should also be monitored in individuals treated with diuretics because these medications can cause hypokalemia, which is associated with cardiovascular risk and mortality (38–40). Individuals with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² receiving ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) should have serum potassium measured periodically to assess for hyperkalemia.
screening_tests.indication: Monitor for hyperkalemia in individuals with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² on ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or MRAs; monitor for hypokalemia when diuretics are used.

screening_tests.name: 10g Monofilament Test
screening_tests.indication: Screen for peripheral neuropathy in the feet.

therapeutic_agents.name: ACE inhibitors
therapeutic_agents.source_text: ACE inhibitors and ARBs should not be discontinued for increases in serum creatinine (<30%) in the absence of volume depletion.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Moderately increased albuminuria (UACR 30–299 mg/g creatinine) or severely increased albuminuria (UACR ≥300 mg/g creatinine) and/or eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m².

therapeutic_agents.name: Angiotensin Receptor Blockers
therapeutic_agents.source_text: ACE inhibitors and ARBs should not be discontinued for increases in serum creatinine (<30%) in the absence of volume depletion.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Moderately increased albuminuria (UACR 30–299 mg/g creatinine) or severely increased albuminuria (UACR ≥300 mg/g creatinine) and/or eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m².

therapeutic_agents.name: SGLT2 inhibitors
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Similar rises in creatinine are seen at the initiation of SGLT2 inhibitors and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) due to hemodynamic changes in the tubuloglomerular feedback, and the medication should not be discontinued.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Type 2 diabetes and CKD with eGFR ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m².

therapeutic_agents.name: Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Similar rises in creatinine are seen at the initiation of SGLT2 inhibitors and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) due to hemodynamic changes in the tubuloglomerular feedback, and the medication should not be discontinued.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Type 2 diabetes and CKD to reduce kidney disease progression and cardiovascular risk.

therapeutic_agents.name: Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Individuals with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² receiving ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) should have serum potassium measured periodically to assess for hyperkalemia.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: CKD and albuminuria to reduce CKD progression and cardiovascular events (if eGFR is ≥25 mL/min/1.73 m²).

therapeutic_agents.name: Finerenone
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Finerenone is currently the only nsMRA with proven clinical kidney and cardiovascular benefits.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: CKD and albuminuria to reduce CKD progression and cardiovascular events (if eGFR is ≥25 mL/min/1.73 m²).

therapeutic_agents.name: Metformin
therapeutic_agents.source_text: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) revised its guidance for the use of metformin in CKD in 2016 (114), recommending use of eGFR instead of serum creatinine to guide treatment and expanding the pool of people with kidney disease for whom metformin treatment should be considered.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Contraindicated in individuals with an eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²; should not be initiated for individuals with an eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73 m².

therapeutic_agents.name: Diuretics
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Monitor for hypokalemia when diuretics are used.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: To attain BP targets, often in combination with ACEi or ARB.

therapeutic_agents.name: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers
therapeutic_agents.source_text: In the absence of kidney disease, ACE inhibitors or ARBs are useful to manage blood pressure but have not proven superior to alternative classes of antihypertensive therapy, including thiazide-like diuretics and dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (93).
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: To attain BP targets, often in combination with ACEi or ARB.

risk_factors.name: Albuminuria
risk_factors.source_text: CKD is diagnosed by the persistent elevation of urinary albumin excretion (albuminuria), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73 m², or other manifestations of kidney damage (1).
risk_factors.impact_magnitude: Increases risk of CKD progression, cardiovascular disease, and mortality.

risk_factors.name: Hypertension
risk_factors.source_text: The only proven primary prevention interventions for CKD in people with diabetes are blood glucose (A1C goal of 7%) and blood pressure management (<130/80 mmHg).
risk_factors.impact_magnitude: Increases risk of CKD progression and cardiovascular disease.

risk_factors.name: Diabetes duration
risk_factors.source_text: CKD in people with diabetes typically develops after a duration of 10 years in type 1 diabetes (the most common presentation is 5–15 years after the diagnosis of type 1 diabetes) but may be present at diagnosis of type 2 diabetes.
risk_factors.impact_magnitude: Longer duration increases risk of CKD.

risk_factors.name: Type 1 Diabetes
risk_factors.source_text: CKD in people with diabetes typically develops after a duration of 10 years in type 1 diabetes (the most common presentation is 5–15 years after the diagnosis of type 1 diabetes) but may be present at diagnosis of type 2 diabetes.
risk_factors.impact_magnitude: CKD develops after a duration of 10 years.

risk_factors.name: Type 2 Diabetes
risk_factors.source_text: CKD in people with diabetes typically develops after a duration of 10 years in type 1 diabetes (the most common presentation is 5–15 years after the diagnosis of type 1 diabetes) but may be present at diagnosis of type 2 diabetes.
risk_factors.impact_magnitude: CKD may be present at diagnosis.

risk_factors.name: eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m²
risk_factors.source_text: CKD is diagnosed by the persistent elevation of urinary albumin excretion (albuminuria), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73 m², or other manifestations of kidney damage (1).
risk_factors.impact_magnitude: Indicates CKD and increases risk of progression and complications.

referral_criteria.name: Referral to Nephrologist for CKD
referral_criteria.source_text: Individuals should be referred for evaluation by a nephrologist if they have rapidly increasing urinary albumin levels and/or rapidly decreasing eGFR and/or if the eGFR is <30 mL/min/1.73 m².
referral_criteria.criteria: Rapidly increasing UACR, rapidly decreasing eGFR, or eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m².

referral_criteria.name: Referral to Nephrologist for uncertain etiology
referral_criteria.source_text: Refer to a nephrologist for uncertainty about the etiology of kidney disease or difficult management issues.
referral_criteria.criteria: Uncertainty about the etiology of kidney disease.

referral_criteria.name: Referral to Nephrologist for difficult management issues
referral_criteria.source_text: Refer to a nephrologist for uncertainty about the etiology of kidney disease or difficult management issues.
referral_criteria.criteria: Difficult management issues (anemia, secondary hyperparathyroidism, significant increases in albuminuria despite good blood pressure management, metabolic bone disease, resistant hypertension, or electrolyte disturbances).

referral_criteria.name: Referral to Nephrologist for advanced CKD
referral_criteria.source_text: Consultation with a nephrologist when stage G4 CKD develops (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²) has been found to reduce cost, improve quality of care, and delay the need for dialysis (159).

referral_criteria.name: Referral to Nephrologist for kidney replacement therapy discussion
referral_criteria.source_text: when there is advanced kidney disease (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²) requiring discussion of kidney replacement therapy for kidney failure (1).
referral_criteria.criteria: Advanced kidney disease (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²) requiring discussion of kidney replacement therapy for kidney failure.
